ENGI 1010.name: Foundations of Programming
ENGI 1010.description: Introduction to computational thinking and programming using a high-level language. Topics include variables, control structures, functions, arrays, and basic algorithms. Students develop problem-solving skills through programming assignments.

ENGI 1020.name: Engineering Statics
ENGI 1020.description: Principles of statics applied to engineering problems. Topics include forces and moments, equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies, trusses, frames, friction, centroids, and moments of inertia.

ENGI 1030.name: Engineering Graphics and Design
ENGI 1030.description: Principles of engineering drawing and design. Topics include orthographic projection, sectional views, dimensioning, tolerancing, and introduction to CAD software. Emphasis on communicating designs clearly through technical drawings.

ENGI 1050.name: Introduction to Circuits
ENGI 1050.description: Fundamentals of electric circuits. Topics include DC circuit analysis using Kirchhoff's laws, node and mesh methods, Thevenin and Norton equivalents, capacitors, inductors, and an introduction to AC circuits.

ENGI 200W.name: Professional Development
ENGI 200W.description: Non-credit course covering professional skills for engineers including technical writing, oral communication, ethics, and workplace readiness. Required for continuation in the engineering program.

MATH 1000.name: Calculus I
MATH 1000.description: Limits, continuity, derivatives of single-variable functions, rules of differentiation, implicit differentiation, related rates, linear approximation, curve sketching, and optimization. Introduction to antiderivatives.

MATH 1001.name: Calculus II
MATH 1001.description: Definite and indefinite integrals, the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, techniques of integration, applications of integration (area, volume, arc length), sequences and series, Taylor series.

MATH 2050.name: Linear Algebra I
MATH 2050.description: Systems of linear equations, matrices, determinants, vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and orthogonality. Applications to engineering problems.

PHYS 1050.name: Physics I
PHYS 1050.description: Classical mechanics: kinematics and dynamics of particles, Newton's laws, work and energy, momentum, rotational motion, oscillations, and gravitation.

PHYS 1051.name: Physics II
PHYS 1051.description: Electricity and magnetism: electric fields, Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitance, current and resistance, magnetic fields, Faraday's law, and introduction to electromagnetic waves.

CHEM 1050.name: Chemistry I
CHEM 1050.description: Fundamental principles of chemistry: atomic theory, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, states of matter, thermochemistry, and introduction to solutions and chemical equilibrium.

ENGL 1090.name: Introduction to Academic Writing
ENGL 1090.description: Development of academic writing skills including essay structure, argumentation, research skills, and citation practices. Students write multiple essays of increasing complexity.

ME 3301.name: Dynamics
ME 3301.description: Kinematics and kinetics of particles and rigid bodies. Topics include rectilinear and curvilinear motion, Newton's laws, work-energy and impulse-momentum methods, and an introduction to vibration.

ME 3102.name: Production Technology
ME 3102.description: Overview of manufacturing processes including casting, forming, machining, welding, and additive manufacturing. Introduces material selection, quality control, and tolerancing concepts.

ENGI 3101.name: Engineering Professionalism I
ENGI 3101.description: Introduction to professional engineering practice including the role of engineers in society, professional ethics and codes of conduct, engineering law, equity and diversity, and technical communication.

ENGI 3424.name: Engineering Mathematics
ENGI 3424.description: Mathematical methods for engineering. Topics include ordinary differential equations, Laplace transforms, Fourier series, partial differential equations, and introductory complex analysis.

ME 3201.name: Thermodynamics I
ME 3201.description: Fundamental concepts of thermodynamics. Topics include properties of pure substances, work and heat interactions, the first and second laws of thermodynamics, entropy, and ideal gas behavior.

ME 3401.name: Materials Science
ME 3401.description: Structure-property relationships in engineering materials. Topics include atomic bonding, crystal structures, phase diagrams, heat treatment, mechanical properties, and an overview of metals, ceramics, and polymers.

ENGI 4430.name: Advanced Calculus for Engineering
ENGI 4430.description: Advanced mathematical methods for engineering. Topics include vector calculus (gradient, divergence, curl), line and surface integrals, Green's and Stokes' theorems, and applications to engineering problems.

ME 4302.name: Mechanisms and Machines
ME 4302.description: Analysis and synthesis of mechanisms. Topics include kinematic analysis of linkages, velocity and acceleration analysis, gear trains, cams, and dynamic analysis of machines.

ME 4402.name: Thermodynamics II
ME 4402.description: Applications of thermodynamics to engineering systems. Topics include thermodynamic cycles (Rankine, Brayton, Otto, Diesel), refrigeration, mixtures and psychrometrics, and combustion fundamentals.

ME 4501.name: Fluid Mechanics I
ME 4501.description: Fundamentals of fluid mechanics. Topics include fluid statics, kinematics, the continuity equation, Bernoulli's equation, the momentum equation, pipe flow, dimensional analysis, and similitude.

ME 4601.name: Mechanics of Solids I
ME 4601.description: Mechanics of deformable bodies. Topics include stress and strain, axial loading, torsion, bending of beams, shear and bending moment diagrams, beam deflection, and introductory failure theories.

ME 5103.description: Advanced study of engineering material behavior. Topics include phase transformations, corrosion, fracture mechanics, fatigue, creep, and selection of materials for mechanical applications.

ENGI 4421.description: Probability theory and statistical methods for engineers. Topics include probability distributions, statistical inference, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and quality control.

ME 5602.name: Mechanics of Solids II
ME 5602.description: Advanced mechanics of materials. Topics include unsymmetrical bending, shear flow, energy methods, yield criteria, plastic deformation, fatigue, and an introduction to fracture mechanics.

ME 5502.description: Advanced fluid mechanics. Topics include viscous flow, boundary layer theory, external flow over bodies, compressible flow fundamentals, and an introduction to turbomachinery.

ONAE 5022.description: Application of stochastic methods to ocean engineering. Topics include random processes, spectral analysis of ocean waves, response of structures to random loading, and reliability fundamentals.

ONAE 5034.name: Marine Vibrations
ONAE 5034.description: Vibration analysis applied to marine structures and machinery. Topics include free and forced vibration, torsional and axial vibrations of shafting, hull vibrations, and noise control in ships.

PHYS 3300.name: Introduction to Physical Oceanography
PHYS 3300.description: Physical properties and dynamics of the ocean. Topics include ocean stratification, currents, tides, waves, sea ice, and the interaction of ocean and atmosphere relevant to marine engineering.

ONAE 6002.name: Ship Structures I
ONAE 6002.description: Analysis and design of ship structural systems. Topics include ship structural loads, hull girder bending and shear, primary, secondary, and tertiary structural elements, and classification society rules.

ONAE 6005.name: Floating Ocean Structures Design
ONAE 6005.description: Design of floating offshore platforms including semi-submersibles, FPSOs, and spars. Topics include environmental loading, hydrostatic stability, mooring systems, and structural design principles.

ONAE 6036.name: Dynamics of Ocean Vehicles
ONAE 6036.description: Dynamics and seakeeping of ships and ocean vehicles. Topics include equations of motion, seakeeping theory, ship responses in waves, ship motion prediction, and operability analysis.

ONAE 6046.name: Marine Engineering Systems
ONAE 6046.description: Ship systems engineering. Topics include electrical power systems, piping and HVAC systems, fire protection, ballast and bilge systems, and integration of marine engineering systems.

ONAE 6055.name: Marine Cybernetics
ONAE 6055.description: Control and automation of marine systems. Topics include dynamic positioning, autopilots, ship manoeuvring models, feedback control design, and integrated bridge systems.

ONAE 7000.name: Ocean Systems Design
ONAE 7000.description: Capstone design project for ocean and naval architectural engineering. Students undertake a complete ship or offshore system design, integrating hydrodynamics, structures, propulsion, and systems engineering.

ONAE 7002.name: Ship Structures II
ONAE 7002.description: Advanced ship structural analysis and design. Topics include fatigue and fracture of marine structures, finite element analysis, ultimate strength of hull girders, and structural assessment methods.

ONAE 7033.name: Marine Hydrodynamics
ONAE 7033.description: Advanced hydrodynamics for marine applications. Topics include potential flow methods, wave-body interactions, added mass and damping, and computational approaches for ship and offshore structure hydrodynamics.

ONAE 7036.name: Manoeuvring of Ocean Vehicles
ONAE 7036.description: Ship manoeuvring theory and control. Topics include mathematical models of ship manoeuvring, hydrodynamic derivatives, rudder and thruster systems, harbour manoeuvring, and dynamic positioning.

ONAE 8600.name: Naval Architecture Design Project II
ONAE 8600.description: Completion of the capstone design project. Teams finalize the design, produce a complete design report to industry standards, and defend their work in a formal presentation.

ENGI 3101.name: Engineering Professionalism I
ENGI 3101.description: Introduction to professional engineering practice including ethics, codes of conduct, engineering law, and technical communication.

ENGI 3424.name: Engineering Mathematics
ENGI 3424.description: Mathematical methods for engineering including ordinary differential equations, Laplace transforms, Fourier series, and partial differential equations.

PROC 3001.name: Material and Energy Balances
PROC 3001.description: Introduction to process engineering principles. Topics include stoichiometry, material balances for reacting and non-reacting systems, energy balances, and an introduction to process flow diagrams.

PROC 3002.name: Introduction to Process Engineering
PROC 3002.description: Foundational concepts in process engineering. Topics include units and dimensions, process variables, equipment overview, safety in process plants, and an introduction to chemical engineering design.

ENGI 4430.name: Advanced Calculus for Engineering
ENGI 4430.description: Advanced mathematical methods for engineering. Topics include vector calculus, line and surface integrals, and applications to process engineering problems.

PROC 4002.name: Process Engineering Thermodynamics
PROC 4002.description: Thermodynamics applied to process systems. Topics include the first and second laws, properties of pure substances and mixtures, vapor-liquid equilibria, equations of state, and thermodynamic cycle analysis.

PROC 4021.name: Process Mathematical Methods
PROC 4021.description: Mathematical methods for process engineering. Topics include ODEs, PDEs, numerical methods, and their application to process modeling and simulation problems.

PROC 4025.name: Process Engineering Calculations
PROC 4025.description: Quantitative methods for process engineering analysis. Topics include reaction stoichiometry, phase equilibria calculations, and steady-state and transient process calculations.

PROC 4061.name: Process Fluid Dynamics I
PROC 4061.description: Fluid mechanics for process engineers. Topics include fluid statics, the continuity and momentum equations, Bernoulli's equation, pipe flow, pumps, and dimensional analysis.

ENGI 4421.name: Probability and Statistics
ENGI 4421.description: Probability theory and statistical methods for engineers. Topics include probability distributions, statistical inference, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and quality control.

PROC 5001.name: Mass Transfer
PROC 5001.description: Principles of mass transfer in process systems. Topics include molecular diffusion, convective mass transfer, absorption, stripping, and distillation column design.

PROC 5002.name: Process Heat Transfer
PROC 5002.description: Heat transfer applied to process engineering. Topics include conduction, convection, radiation, heat exchangers (shell-and-tube, plate), and thermal design of process equipment.

PROC 5071.name: Process Equipment Design I
PROC 5071.description: Mechanical design of process equipment. Topics include pressure vessel theory, design to ASME standards, material selection, nozzle and flange design, and fabrication methods.

PROC 5092.name: Chemistry and Physics of Engineering Materials
PROC 5092.description: Properties and behavior of engineering materials in process environments. Topics include corrosion mechanisms, material degradation, alloy selection, and non-metallic materials for process applications.

PROC 6025.name: Process Modelling and Analysis
PROC 6025.description: Development and analysis of mathematical models for process systems. Topics include steady-state and dynamic process models, process simulation software (e.g. HYSYS, Aspen), and model validation.

PROC 6031.name: Chemical Reaction Engineering
PROC 6031.description: Design of chemical reactors. Topics include reaction kinetics, ideal reactor types (batch, CSTR, PFR), reactor sizing, temperature effects, multiple reactions, and non-ideal flow.

PROC 6061.name: Process Fluid Dynamics II
PROC 6061.description: Advanced fluid mechanics for process systems. Topics include compressible flow, non-Newtonian fluids, multiphase flow, fluidization, and flow assurance in pipelines.

PROC 6071.name: Process Equipment Design II
PROC 6071.description: Advanced design of process equipment. Topics include design of distillation columns, absorbers, heat exchangers, reactors, and storage tanks with emphasis on process integration and optimization.

PROC 7021.name: Process Dynamics and Control
PROC 7021.description: Dynamic modeling and control of chemical processes. Topics include Laplace domain analysis, PID control tuning, cascade and feedforward control, stability analysis, and process control instrumentation.

PROC 7040.name: Process Engineering Project I
PROC 7040.description: First phase of a two-term capstone design project. Student teams undertake a complete process plant design including process selection, simulation, preliminary equipment sizing, and safety analysis.

PROC 7077.name: Process Plant Design and Economics
PROC 7077.description: Integrated process plant design and economic analysis. Topics include process flow diagrams, P&IDs, capital cost estimation, profitability analysis, and economic optimization of process designs.

PROC 8600.name: Process Engineering Project II
PROC 8600.description: Completion of the capstone design project. Teams produce a full process design package including detailed P&IDs, economic analysis, environmental assessment, and a professional presentation.
